'''Clinton Anthony John Duffy''' (born c. 1966) is a [[New Zealand]] marine scientist, who works in the Marine Conservation Unit of the [[Department of Conservation (New Zealand)|Department of Conservation]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/science/news/article.cfm?c_id=82&objectid=10560451&pnum=0|title=Scientists get their teeth into shark preservation|last=Cumming |first=Geoff |date=7 March 2009|work=The New Zealand Herald|accessdate=17 February 2010}}</ref> Duffy is a shark expert, whose work  includes the [[Taxonomy (biology)|taxonomy]] and conservation status of New Zealand's deepwater [[Squaliformes|dogfishes]], attaching [[GPS wildlife tracking]] devices to great white sharks,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=10553492|title=Hunt on for man-eaters|last=Rorke |first=Claire |date=25 January 2009|work=The New Zealand Herald|accessdate=17 February 2010}}</ref> and surveying [[basking shark]]s.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/the-press/news/3236101/Scientists-survey-basking-sharks|title=Scientists survey basking sharks |last=Gorman|first=Paul|date=18 January 2010|work=The Press|accessdate=17 February 2010}}</ref>

He performed the public dissection of a great white shark at the [[Auckland Museum]] in 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/787661|title=Great white shark opened up to the public |date=8 January 2009|work=Stuff.co.nz|accessdate=17 February 2010}}</ref>

Duffy has BSc and MSc degrees from the [[University of Canterbury]].
